subject: MedFlux post-demo: integration checkpoints, compliance, and next steps
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@medflux.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: MedFlux post-demo: integration checkpoints, compliance, and next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so we have alignment before we move to a PoC.

Top pain points you reiterated:
- Live triage agents need sub-200ms turn latency for suggestions at 99th percentile.
- Relevance drift when using existing in-house embeddings for domain-specific notes.
- PHI-sensitive fields need deterministic redaction prior to any third-party inference.
- Volume spikiness (bursty 10–15x peak) during morning rounds.

Goals we heard:
- Pilot a hybrid flow where local pre-processing (PHI redaction + indexing) happens in your VPC, then lightweight embedding + rerank is done via Redwood Dedicated, aiming for 300 QPS sustained with <120ms 95p generation latency.
- Preserve audit logs and per-request user id for traceability.
- Evaluate model variants for accuracy vs cost tradeoffs.

Integration-focused technical checkpoints (what we discussed):
1) SDK adapt: Introduce a streaming+funcall path in the agent SDK to allow early token-level suggestions and structured JSON outputs (for downstream auto-fill). We’ll provide a small shim for your JS agent to call Redwood streaming endpoints.
2) Function calling: We’ll model structured outputs as explicit funcalls (JSON schema) so your front-end can safely map fields for EHR forms; we discussed a limited schema to start (patient_id, snippet, suggested_action).
3) Embeddings + rerank: Recommend a candidate reranking step — coarse embedding search in your infra (to keep PHI local) and a lightweight reranker on Redwood with fused attention quantization for latency.
4) Prefix/KV caching: We'll enable per-conversation KV caching to cut token costs and improve latency for repeated context.

Constraints / blockers you raised:
- Must pass a minimal security checklist (SOC2 evidence + enclave/network diagram).
- Procurement needs an approximate TCV and a 60‑day review before PO.

Attachments: medflux-poc-sow.pdf (draft SOW), embed-stream-sequence-diagram.png (flow diagram).

Proposed next steps (owner / timing):
- You: Share a sanitized sample of 500 clinical notes for latency & rerank evaluation (target: Thu 2/19).
- Redwood (Ben): Deliver a draft PoC plan and ballpark TCV for the pilot (by Fri 2/20).
- Redwood (Kim): Schedule a technical deep-dive with engineering to lock on API hooks and schema (60-min, propose Mon/Tue next week).

If that matches your readout, I’ll open the PoC workbook in HubSpot and send a proposed calendar for the deep-dive.

Thanks — Mateo

Thanks Mateo — that is helpful and accurate. A couple small clarifications from our side:

- PHI redaction: We need to keep all raw clinical notes inside our VPC. Any embedding or rerank candidate generation that leaves the VPC must be on de-identified text. We can provide a deterministic redaction script (or you can run a Redwood redaction container in our VPC).
- On‑prem / VPC option: Evaluating Redwood Dedicated + a private control plane is a hard requirement for our procurement team; can you outline the minimal footprint for a Dedicated pool to support 300 QPS?
- Compliance packet: Attaching SOC2 report (redacted) and point-of-contact for security reviews is sec@medflux.ai. Procurement is on a 6–8 week review cadence (may be 60 days) — we’ll escalate once we have a draft SOW and ballpark pricing.

Tentative go/no-go is late March assuming PoC validates latency and accuracy.

Olivia Chen
Head of Product, MedFlux Health

Olivia — following up with the commercial side and a short mutual action plan. High level:

1) Pilot scope: 8-week PoC — ingest sanitized dataset (you provide), integration of streaming SDK + function-calling for structured outputs, rerank evaluation for clinical recall.
2) Estimated pilot cost (ballpark): $28k–$40k USD for Dedicated pilot footprint (includes burst capacity for morning spikes and observability retention). Exact number depends on days/weeks of reserved capacity we configure.
3) Procurement checklist: PO to Redwood, SOC2 + network diagram review, standard DPA (we can push our standard), and a short MSA amendment for PHI handling.

- Ben: Upload draft PoC mutual action plan to HubSpot and include the SOW you received (today EOD).
